summary: ORCA three-class annotation contract: carcinoma, heterogeneous non-carcinoma tissue, and immutable non-tissue fragments.

annotation_traits: non-tissue can occur as fragmented holes or islands inside a patch
semantic_limitations: Other tissue is mixed non-carcinoma tissue and must not be interpreted as pure stroma, immune, mucosa, muscle, salivary gland, vessel, or normal epithelium.
ORCA does not encode a reason for non-tissue fragmentation; every zero pixel remains protected.

rules.claim: Treat Other tissue only as ORCA non-carcinoma tissue; do not infer a histologic subtype that the mask does not encode.
rules.required_observation: Use H&E to judge local plausibility while retaining the coarse source label in the edit contract.
exceptions: A separately versioned annotation source may add a reviewed tissue subtype without changing the ORCA mask.
counterexamples: Calling all gray pixels stroma and allowing a stroma-specific primitive.
Treating muscle or salivary tissue within Other tissue as interchangeable with desmoplastic stroma.
expected_morphology: A candidate follows a visible carcinoma/non-carcinoma interface whose H&E context supports the requested direction.
forbidden_morphology: An edit justified only by the gray class color without H&E compatibility.
known_limitations: The public class contract does not subdivide non-carcinoma tissue.

rules.claim: Every native non-tissue pixel, including small internal fragments, is immutable and cannot seed, receive, connect, or be crossed by Tumor or Other tissue edits.
rules.required_observation: Compare source and candidate masks at native-zero pixels and verify selected source/target component IDs are nonzero scene components.
counterexamples: Using a one-pixel background fragment as the seed for tumor growth.
Filling scattered zero holes with tumor during morphological closing.
Bridging two tumor lobes across a thin non-tissue gap.
Converting zero pixels to Other tissue before expanding tumor.
expected_morphology: All original non-tissue fragments are pixel-identical after editing.
forbidden_morphology: Hole filling, background swallowing, or cross-background bridges.
known_limitations: Fragmentation thresholds must be measured from the mounted dataset; the invariant itself does not depend on a threshold.

rules.claim: Start burden edits only from an existing carcinoma/non-carcinoma-tissue interface and keep the entire edit within the connected tissue support on the selected side.
rules.required_observation: Confirm interface adjacency in the source mask and confirm on H&E that both sides are tissue rather than whitespace, tear, fold, or lumen.
counterexamples: Starting tumor growth from an isolated point inside gray tissue.
Selecting a black/gray edge as if it were a carcinoma interface.
expected_morphology: The changed band remains attached to one selected carcinoma boundary segment.
forbidden_morphology: Remote islands or edits initiated from non-tissue boundaries.
known_limitations: H&E artifact recognition requires multimodal review.

rules.claim: A local burden edit must not create a new tumor island, split source tissue, merge separated tumor components, or introduce/fill a hole.
rules.required_observation: Compare connected components and holes for source and target labels before and after editing.
exceptions: A dedicated, explicitly requested topology-changing primitive with its own reviewed contract.
counterexamples: A narrow bridge merging separate carcinoma components.
A detached carcinoma island inside Other tissue.
A regression cut splitting one carcinoma nest in two.
expected_morphology: Boundary displacement preserves pre-edit component relationships.
forbidden_morphology: New islands, holes, component splits, or merges.
known_limitations: Topology-changing instructions are outside the v1 primitive set.

rules.claim: Do not infer ORCA from organ or color alone; require an explicit profile ID, preprocessing revision, and label-map digest.
rules.required_observation: Validate declared profile metadata and native-to-canonical remap provenance before planning.
counterexamples: Assuming every oral SCC mask uses ORCA conventions.
Applying ORCA semantics to an unlabeled 0/1/2 mask by visual color.
known_limitations: The repository has not yet mounted a complete immutable ORCA evidence manifest.
